title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on ‘Suspected Money Mule Accounts to Prevent Cyber-enabled Financial Frauds’
summary: The Reserve Bank had issued the draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 on September 11, 2026, for seeking feedback from stakeholders. The draft Amendment Directions proposed a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) laying down a uniform, time-bound procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds, and to remove such holds in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience. 2. Feedback received on the above draft Directions has been examined and the consequent modifications have been suitably incorporated in the final Amendment Directions. A statement on the feedback received is provided in the Annex . Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following Amendment Directions, which shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or from such earlier date as a bank may decide to implement the SOP. title: Thirty First Meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to Review the Flow of Credit to the MSME Sector in Kolkata on November 27, 2026
summary: The 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to review the flow of credit to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) was held in Kolkata on November 27, 2026. Shri Swaminathan J, Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India (RBI), chaired the meeting. Participants included the Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, and the Joint Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. Managing directors and executive directors of select banks, heads of SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC and KVIC, the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Banks’ Association, and representatives of national, regional and state-level MSME associations also attended. Recognising MSMEs’ contribution to India’s economy and development goals, the Deputy Governor urged banks to expedite credit sanctions and reduce reliance on collateral through cash-flow-based lending using ULI and other digital channels. He called for greater use of TReDS for receivables financing and early identification and resolution of stress. title: Services domestic regulation disciplines enter into force for Kazakhstan
summary: On 25 November, Kazakhstan notified WTO members that, following conclusion of its domestic approval procedures, the disciplines on services domestic regulation had taken legal effect and had been incorporated into Kazakhstan's schedule under the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) as of 27 October 2026. These disciplines, which entered into force at the 13th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC13) in February 2024, have the potential to reduce global trade costs by USD 127 billion.
